name: Email Delivery Agent
description: Owner-controlled email delivery. Sending an email is an external write, so the application holds the send step until a person decides on its publish card: the card shows the rows the send step declares (the sending mailbox, the recipients, the emails and the call to action), and the run reaches the send only after the person chose to send. The flow draws no confirmation of its own. A read-only prepare step reports the counts and the content digest of the pending send, a filing step files one recipient record per confirmed recipient, a read step resolves the approved draft bundle and the confirmed recipient list (the two references the send start reads) into the recipients and the email bodies the send mails, which are the values the card shows, and the send itself is a model-free call of email_outreach_send_initial_start on the passthrough road, whose arguments are the flow's values: the sender and the two references from the start, and the approved bodies the card showed from the read step. The run ends with one plain sentence on the send start's answer.

inputs.title: emailBodies
inputs.description: The approved email bodies: the artifact revision of each draft's approved body. Each one names the contact of its draft (the draft's contactId, else its recipientId), or, when none names a contact, they are one for each draft of the approved draft bundle, in draft order. The read step joins each one to its draft, compares it with the body of that draft and refuses a body it cannot join to exactly one draft; the publish card shows those of the drafts the send mails, and the send mails their text.

inputs.title: callToAction
inputs.description: The call to action of the emails. A run without it does not start. The read step hands it on to the publish card only when the text of every body the send mails carries it, and ends the run before the card otherwise.

outputs.title: sendStatus
outputs.description: The status the send start answered: completed, or failed; the empty string when no send ran.

outputs.title: sentCount
outputs.description: The number of campaign emails the send start reports as sent.

outputs.title: sendErrorMessage
outputs.description: What stopped a failed send; the empty string otherwise.

data.system: You are the email-delivery agent's PRE-SEND summarizer. You do NOT send anything. You MUST objects_get ALL THREE records: the approved draft bundle (approvedDraftBundleRef), the confirmed recipient set (confirmedRecipientsRef), and the campaign record (campaignId, to determine its scheduled send time). Then return a SINGLE JSON object with exactly two top-level keys, "summary" and "contentDigest". "summary": { "recipientCount": <integer number of confirmed recipients ACTUALLY loaded from confirmedRecipientsRef>, "draftCount": <integer number of approved drafts ACTUALLY in the loaded bundle>, "scheduledAt": <the campaign's scheduled send time as an ISO-8601 string when the campaign record shows it is scheduled for the future, otherwise the empty string ""> }. Count ONLY from the records you actually loaded — NEVER guess, estimate, or emit placeholder numbers. FAIL VISIBLE: if a ref cannot be read, set that count to 0; never leave a summary key out, because all three keys are required, and never substitute a guessed or placeholder number. After the three reads, call email_outreach_send_initial_preview exactly once, with exactly { "approvedDraftBundleRef": <the approvedDraftBundleRef input>, "confirmedRecipientsRef": <the confirmedRecipientsRef input> } and no other key. It is a read-only tool: it sends nothing and returns { draftCount, recipientCount, contentDigest }. "contentDigest": <the contentDigest string exactly as the tool returned it, character for character>. NEVER compute, shorten, re-encode or invent a digest. If the tool is not offered, fails or returns no contentDigest, set "contentDigest" to the empty string "". Use objects_get and email_outreach_send_initial_preview ONLY; do not call any send, save, update, or other write tool. This step reports the REAL recipient/draft counts of the pending send and its content digest.

outputs.title: summary
outputs.description: The pre-send summary of the pending send, the step's own output. Every member is always present: the structured-output contract the runtime derives from this declaration carries no optional key, so an unreadable ref is reported as a count of 0 and an unscheduled campaign as the empty string.

recipientCount.description: Confirmed recipients actually loaded from confirmedRecipientsRef.

draftCount.description: Approved drafts actually loaded from approvedDraftBundleRef.

scheduledAt.description: The campaign's scheduled send time as an ISO-8601 string, or the empty string when it is not scheduled for the future.

outputs.title: contentDigest
outputs.description: The content digest the read-only preview tool returned for the approved draft bundle and the confirmed recipients, unchanged; the empty string when the preview returned none. It is this step's own output: the send step does not pass it on, because the send start mails the approved body revisions the publish card showed. This flow does not check the digest itself: refusing a send whose bodies changed after the person decided is left to the application's send start, which reads each approved body revision when the send starts and refuses one that is no longer current.

cinatra.description: Read-only pre-send summarizer. Reads all three records, approvedDraftBundleRef, confirmedRecipientsRef and the campaign record (campaignId), via the injected Cinatra self-MCP objects_get, calls the read-only email_outreach_send_initial_preview once, and returns { summary: { recipientCount, draftCount, scheduledAt }, contentDigest }: the counts computed only from the records it actually loaded (a count of 0 when a ref cannot be read), the digest exactly as the preview returned it (the empty string when it returned none). metadata.cinatra.toolboxes is INTENTIONALLY OMITTED so the default always-inject path reaches objects_get. This node performs NO write. Its summary and its contentDigest are the step's own outputs.

file_recipients.name: File one record per confirmed recipient

cinatra.description: The agent files one recipient record per confirmed recipient of this run, keyed by the run and the contact, with the address only where one exists, before the send. The records are kept inside Cinatra, so this step makes no external write. A record that is refused ends the run before the send.

input.emailBodies: {# pyagentspec-input-hint (do not remove): {{ emailBodies }} #}{{ emailBodies | tojson }}

outputs.title: recipients
outputs.description: One line per draft the send mails: the name, the address the send start addresses it to, and the company. When the workspace's development-mode recipient override is on, the email pipeline mails the override address instead; this list does not show it.

outputs.title: emailBodies
outputs.description: The approved body of each draft the send mails, in draft order: its artifact revision, compared with the body of its draft, and the contact of that draft. The send step passes this list to the send start as approvedBodies, and the publish card's Emails row shows it.

outputs.title: callToAction
outputs.description: The call to action the run names, trimmed, handed on only when the text of every body the send mails carries it. The publish card's Call to action row shows it.

cinatra.description: The agent reads the approved draft bundle and the confirmed recipient list, the same two references the send step passes to the send start, and resolves them into what the send mails: the recipients (the address of each draft as the send chooses it) and the approved bodies (the body revision the run hands in for each mailed draft, joined to that draft by its contact or, when the bodies name no contact, by its position in the bundle, compared with the body of that draft, with the draft's contact). The send step takes the recipients and the bodies from this step only and passes the bodies to the send start as approvedBodies, so the publish card shows what the send mails. It also hands on the call to action the card's Call to action row shows, and only one that the text of every mailed body carries, so the card never shows a call to action the send does not mail. A body that cannot be joined to exactly one draft or is not the body of its draft, a mailed draft without a body or a contact, one contact or one artifact named twice, more than 50 mailed drafts, a bundle with nothing to mail, a run without a call to action (CALL_TO_ACTION_MISSING) or a mailed body without it (CALL_TO_ACTION_NOT_IN_EMAIL) ends the run before the card. This step writes nothing.

input.approvedBodies: {# pyagentspec-input-hint (do not remove): {{ emailBodies }} {{ recipients }} {{ callToAction }} #}{{ emailBodies | tojson }}

inputs.title: recipients
inputs.description: The recipients the send mails, as the read step resolved them from the approved draft bundle and the confirmed recipient list: one line per mailed draft with its name, email and company. These are the addresses the send start addresses; when the workspace's development-mode recipient override is on, the email pipeline mails the override address instead, which the card's Recipients row does not show

inputs.title: emailBodies
inputs.description: The approved email bodies the send mails, as the read step joined them to the approved drafts: one artifact revision and the contact of its draft per mailed draft. The publish card's Emails row shows this list and the send start receives it as approvedBodies

inputs.title: callToAction
inputs.description: The call to action of the emails, as the read step handed it on after it found it in the text of every body the send mails; the publish card shows it

outputs.title: status
outputs.description: The status the send start answered: completed, or failed when the send stopped; the empty string when the answer carried none.

outputs.title: sentCount
outputs.description: The number of messages the send start reports as sent.

outputs.title: operationId
outputs.description: The operation identifier the send start answered.

outputs.title: errorMessage
outputs.description: What stopped a failed send, as the send start answered it; the empty string for a completed send.

cinatra.description: The flow's one publishing step and a model-free call of email_outreach_send_initial_start on the deterministic passthrough road (/api/agents/passthrough). Sending an email is an external write, so the application stops the run in front of this step and shows its publish card with the four rows declared here (From, Recipients, Emails, Call to action); the run reaches the step only after the person chose to send. Every argument of the call is a template over one of this step's inputs, and every input comes by a data edge from the start node or from the read step in front of this step: the campaign, the sender and the two references from the start node, and approvedBodies, the list the card's Emails row shows, from the read step, as JSON text. No model writes an argument, so the send start mails the approved body revisions the person saw, from the mailbox the card showed, and refuses the whole send before any mail when one of them does not fit its draft. The passthrough road serves the send start only to a listed publishing step of the run's flow whose publish decision is released, once; a host whose road does not serve it answers the call with an error, the run ends and nothing is sent. The step returns the send start's answer: its status (completed or failed), the number of messages sent, the operation id and, for a failed send, the reason. requiresApproval is false because the publish card is the one approval in front of the send.

delivery_summary.name: Delivery result
delivery_summary.message: {# pyagentspec-input-hint (do not remove): {{ status }} {{ sentCount }} {{ errorMessage }} #}{% if status == 'completed' %}{% if sentCount == 1 %}1 campaign email was sent.{% elif sentCount %}{{ sentCount }} campaign emails were sent.{% else %}The send finished, but no campaign email went out.{% endif %}{% elif status == 'failed' %}{% if errorMessage %}The campaign emails could not be sent: {{ errorMessage }}{% else %}The campaign emails could not be sent, and the send gave no reason.{% endif %}{% else %}No campaign email was sent in this run.{% endif %}
